name: presidents/roster
note: One entry per presidency (Cleveland and Trump each appear twice, as the official numbering counts them).

presidents.name: George Washington
presidents.note: Led the Continental Army, then became the first president and set the two-term tradition.

presidents.name: John Adams
presidents.note: Helped write the case for independence and was the first president to live in the White House.

presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
presidents.note: Wrote the Declaration of Independence and bought the Louisiana Territory.

presidents.name: James Madison
presidents.note: Called the Father of the Constitution; led the country in the War of 1812.

presidents.name: James Monroe
presidents.note: Warned Europe to stay out of the Americas in the Monroe Doctrine.

presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
presidents.note: Son of John Adams; later fought slavery in Congress.

presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
presidents.note: War of 1812 general who called himself the people's president.

presidents.name: Martin Van Buren
presidents.note: The first president born a citizen of the United States.

presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
presidents.note: Gave the longest inaugural address and served only 31 days.

presidents.name: John Tyler
presidents.note: The first vice president to become president when a president died.
presidents.no_inaugural: Became president when William Henry Harrison died, so he gave no inaugural address.

presidents.name: James K. Polk
presidents.note: The country grew west to the Pacific while he was president.

presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
presidents.note: A general in the Mexican–American War who died in office.

presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
presidents.note: Became president when Taylor died; signed the Compromise of 1850.
presidents.no_inaugural: Became president when Zachary Taylor died, so he gave no inaugural address.

presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
presidents.note: Signed the Kansas–Nebraska Act, which deepened the split over slavery.

presidents.name: James Buchanan
presidents.note: President as Southern states began to leave the Union.

presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
presidents.note: Led the Union through the Civil War and worked to end slavery.

presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
presidents.note: Became president after Lincoln was killed; the first president impeached.
presidents.no_inaugural: Became president when Lincoln was killed, so he gave no inaugural address.

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.note: The Union's top general in the Civil War.

presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
presidents.note: His presidency ended Reconstruction in the South.

presidents.name: James A. Garfield
presidents.note: Shot a few months into his term; died that September.

presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
presidents.note: Signed a law so many government jobs went to people who passed tests.
presidents.no_inaugural: Became president when Garfield died, so he gave no inaugural address.

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
presidents.note: The only president to serve two terms that were not back to back (22nd and 24th).

presidents.name: Benjamin Harrison
presidents.note: Grandson of William Henry Harrison; six states joined while he was president.

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
presidents.note: Back for a second, separate term — counted twice.

presidents.name: William McKinley
presidents.note: President during the Spanish–American War; shot in 1901.

presidents.name: Theodore Roosevelt
presidents.note: Protected millions of acres of forests and parks; started the Panama Canal.

presidents.name: William Howard Taft
presidents.note: Later became Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
presidents.note: Led the country in World War I.

presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
presidents.note: Promised a return to normal life after the war; died in office.

presidents.name: Calvin Coolidge
presidents.note: Known as Silent Cal for saying few words.

presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
presidents.note: President when the Great Depression began.

presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
presidents.note: Elected four times; led through the Great Depression and World War II.

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.note: Ended World War II and helped rebuild Europe.

presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
presidents.note: Commanded the D-Day invasion; built the interstate highways.

presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
presidents.note: Set the goal of landing a person on the Moon.

presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
presidents.note: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

presidents.name: Richard Nixon
presidents.note: Opened ties with China; the only president to resign.

presidents.name: Gerald Ford
presidents.note: The only president never elected president or vice president.
presidents.no_inaugural: Became president when Nixon resigned; he spoke to the nation but gave no inaugural address.

presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
presidents.note: Helped make peace between Egypt and Israel at Camp David.

presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
presidents.note: Former actor and governor; president as the Cold War neared its end.

presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
presidents.note: President when the Berlin Wall fell and during the Gulf War.

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
presidents.note: President during a long run of economic growth in the 1990s.

presidents.name: George W. Bush
presidents.note: Son of George H. W. Bush; president on September 11, 2001.

presidents.name: Barack Obama
presidents.note: The first African American president.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.note: Businessman who became president without holding office before.

presidents.name: Joe Biden
presidents.note: Served 36 years in the Senate and was vice president before.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.note: Returned for a second, separate term — counted twice, like Cleveland.
